notable_absence.finding: The 'App Services?' column marks which GCP regions support App Services alongside the base operational cluster - a genuine region-scoped feature-availability constraint specific to GCP's region list (roughly 2/3 of listed regions support it). No predicate in the registry cleanly expresses 'feature X is unavailable in region Y of provider Z' as distinct from the plan-tier and edition gates already modeled; left unmodeled rather than force a relation onto a table column with no single quotable evidence sentence.

cross_component_finding: GCP's storage-speed mechanics are stated as a pure function of disk size ('PD-SSDs receive 30 read and 30 write IOPS per GB provisioned... Increasing the storage to 100 GB increases the maximum read speed to 3000 IOPS') with no separate configurability knob - this is a genuinely different mechanic from AWS (independently configurable IOPS within a range per volume type) and Azure (fixed-by-disk-type for Premium SSD, separately configurable for Ultra Disk only). All three are infrastructure-inherent facts about the underlying disk technology rather than a Capella product decision, so none of the three is modeled as behavesDifferentlyUnder here - that predicate is reserved in this batch for clusters:storage-auto-expansion, where the difference is explicitly about Capella's own operational behavior (node replacement required) rather than a raw hardware spec. Net verdict on this round's hypothesis: aws.md/azure.md/gcp.md are overwhelmingly infrastructure/networking reference (regions, compute, disk types, IOPS) exactly as expected, but they are not ontology-free - the storage-auto-expansion finding (see azure.json) is a real, evidenced within-Capella cloud-provider behavioral axis, independently corroborated by an AWS-specific caveat found on event-reference.md ('Cluster Storage Not Increased... due to AWS limits').
